title: Q1 Market Recap: How Private Credit, AI, & War Have Dominated 2026 So Far | The Weekly Wrap

metadata.title: Q1 Market Recap: How Private Credit, AI, & War Have Dominated 2026 So Far | The Weekly Wrap

summary: The quarter review links software repricing to private-equity and credit risk, criticizes smoothed private valuations, and separates attractive new lending from legacy exposures. Eisman retains Meritage with a specific year-end buyback expectation and an explicit interest-rate caveat. He expects software incumbents to survive but lose seat and pricing momentum. His universal claim that every 2018-2022 PE software deal is underwater lacks transaction-level support; announced layoffs do not independently establish AI unemployment.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
framework_points: Smooth marks do not erase economic volatility.
Separate new lending terms from old-fund recoveries.
Use index weights to understand contribution without confusing stock values and GDP.
Separate software survival from pricing power.
Consider incentives and the timing of credit deterioration.
tools_and_charts: Q1 returns across eleven S&P sectors.
Meritage tangible book and buyback target.
transcript_cautions: Full transcript read including sponsor gap and all mailbags.
AI layoff list combines company announcements without establishing common causation.
Energy-war forecast is conditional on a real resolution, not every temporary truce.

claims.claim: Iran ceasefire uncertainty means markets will keep reacting to war headlines.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: No defined direction, event window or magnitude makes the claim a discriminating market forecast.
claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

claims.claim: Private-equity growth partly reflects appraisal smoothing that flatters reported Sharpe ratios; infrequent marks do not eliminate economic risk, and leverage benefited from low rates.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare unsmoothed asset returns, leverage, reporting lags, cash flows and investor allocation decisions by vintage.
claims.reason: Regulators support valuation opacity and leverage concerns. The exact causal contribution to asset-class growth and the assertion that all PE is equally volatile as public assets are not established.

evidence.title: FSB warns on private-credit vulnerabilities
evidence.finding: Identifies opaque valuations, lower-quality leveraged borrowers, sector concentration, layered leverage and bank/insurer linkages; notes rising PIK and some defaults. Report emphasizes data gaps and does not predict a completed systemic crisis.

claims.next_check: Compare unsmoothed asset returns, leverage, reporting lags, cash flows and investor allocation decisions by vintage.

claims.claim: Extreme withdrawal requests and 5% fulfillment caps at Blue Owl and Carlyle funds signal a serious liquidity-confidence problem.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect original tender filings, share-class denominators, requested versus accepted withdrawals and fund liquidity; gates are not themselves defaults.
claims.reason: The mechanism is plausible, but the specific magnitude, causal attribution or outcome has not been established by inspected primary evidence.
claims.next_check: Inspect original tender filings, share-class denominators, requested versus accepted withdrawals and fund liquidity; gates are not themselves defaults.

claims.claim: Widening credit spreads can make new private-credit lending attractive, helping explain large institutional fundraising despite problems in old funds.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.qualifications: The particular $10b fundraise totals require original sponsor records; a new fund does not rescue the old one.
claims.reason: The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.

assumptions: Expected losses, fees and covenants do not worsen enough to offset them
evidence_basis.derivation: Expected net return equals promised income less expected credit losses and costs. A higher spread improves expected return only holding these other terms sufficiently constant.

claims.claim: Every PE software acquisition from 2018-2022 is now underwater, leaving equity losses and private-credit exposure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect transaction-level entry values, leverage, cash flows, dividends and current independent valuations; a sector stock decline cannot substantiate every deal.
claims.reason: The universal conclusion is unsupported and ignores deal timing, operating growth, leverage and realized distributions. Treat it as a material overgeneralization, not a verified industry loss rate.
claims.next_check: Inspect transaction-level entry values, leverage, cash flows, dividends and current independent valuations; a sector stock decline cannot substantiate every deal.

claims.claim: By mid 2007 toxic assets already made the crisis effectively unavoidable; intervention needed to alter 2005 underwriting, when volume incentives overwhelmed anecdotal warnings.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect contemporaneous loan vintages, institutional exposures and policy alternatives; inevitability is a counterfactual, not a directly observable result.
claims.reason: The incentive mechanism is plausible, but the absolute claim that no action after mid 2007 could avert crisis cannot be established from the evidence supplied.
claims.next_check: Inspect contemporaneous loan vintages, institutional exposures and policy alternatives; inevitability is a counterfactual, not a directly observable result.
